CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF SILVER-TIN DENTAL AMALGAM ALLOY-METHOD
(First Revision)
1 SCOPE
This standard describes the methods for determination of silver, tin, copper and zinc in the dental amalgam alloy in the ranges given below:

5.3.1 Weigh accurately 0.50 g of the sample into a 200 ml beaker and over with a watch glass. Add a mixture of 15 ml of nitric acid and 10 ml of water
by removing the watch glass and replace it immediately. When -the vigorous action is over, evaporate the solution for a -period of at least I h on a steam-bath to a syrupy consistency. Dilute to about I50 ml with dilute nitric acid (I :99) and heat on a water-bath for 30 mirk. 53.2 Allow the precipitate to settle overnight.

Transfer the clear solution over a medium lcxturcd filter paper containing a little ashless filter pulp, retaining the precipitate in the beaker. Wash the residue in the beaker thrice with IO ml portions 01 the hot dilute nitric acid (1:99) and transfer the residue to the filter paper. Wash the residue _furthcr at least five times with hot dilute nitric acid (I :99).
NOTE Every precautions should be taken In avoid contaminalion by chloride in order lo prevent rhe precipirnrion of silver chloride.

Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade rcagcnts and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be employed for the tests. 4 SAMPLING The sample is in the form of fillings or shavings. If in the form of shavings the sample shall be cut into small pieces and shall then be gone over by a magnet to remove extraneous iron. It shall be thoroughly mixed, quartered and then drawn. 5

53.3 Place the filter paper along with the rcsiduc in a weighed silica crucible. Dry carefully and char the filter paper at a low temperature and finally ignite the residue for 30 min in a muftle furnace at about 8OO'C. 53.4 Moisten the precipitate with two drops ol nitric acid (dilute). Evaporate and ignite again. Allow to cool in a dessicator and weigh. Rcpcat the ignition till constant mass is obtained. 53.5 Mix the precipitate with IS times its mass 01 pure ammonium iodide and heat in a mufllc furnace a( 425 to 475�C till no further fumes arc cvolvcd and tin volatilizes completely.
